chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubaid, from Salih ibn Muhammad, from Hani al-Tammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'There will be an occultation for the master of this affair. The one who holds fast to his religion during it is like the one rubbing his hands on a thorny branch.' Then he gestured with his hand and said: 'Like this. Which of you can hold the thorns of the qattad (a thorny shrub) in his hand?' Then he said: 'There will be an occultation for the master of this affair, so let a servant of Allah fear God and hold fast to his religion.'

key_terms.الْقَتَّاد: Qattad (a type of thorny shrub used in the metaphor)
key_terms.الْمُمْسِكُ بِدِينِهِ: The one who holds fast to his religion
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Affair (referring to Imam al-Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor used for holding fast to religion during the Imam's occultation?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) employs the vivid metaphor of a palm frond cutter (*kharit*) enduring the prickly thorns of the *qattad* tree to illustrate the spiritual resilience required during the Major Occultation (*al-Ghayba al-Kubra*). This imagery underscores that while holding onto faith amidst the trials of the unseen Imam is painful and demanding, it yields immense reward, urging believers to actively guard their religious identity against the distractions of the era.
